rules.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
rules.description: Sanitizing an HTTP request parameter may be ineffective if the user controls its type.
Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.

rules.cwe_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
rules.description: Server-side URL redirection based on unvalidated user input may cause redirection to malicious web sites.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Client-side URL redirection based on unvalidated user input may cause redirection to malicious web sites.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
rules.description: Conditions that the user controls are not suited for making security-related decisions.
Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.
Passing identical, or seemingly identical, operands to an operator such as subtraction or conjunction may indicate a typo; even if it is intentional, it makes the code hard to read.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If the id of an HTML attribute is malformed, its interpretation may be browser-dependent.
If the same expression occurs on both sides of a comparison operator, the operator is redundant, and probably indicates a mistake.

rules.cwe_name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
rules.description: Sanitizing an HTTP request parameter may be ineffective if the user controls its type.
Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.
An equality comparison between two values that cannot be meaningfully converted to the same type will always yield 'false', and an inequality comparison will always yield 'true'.
Passing identical, or seemingly identical, operands to an operator such as subtraction or conjunction may indicate a typo; even if it is intentional, it makes the code hard to read.
Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.
An array index is compared to be less than or equal to the 'length' property, and then used in an indexing operation that could be out of bounds.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
rules.description: Conditions that the user controls are not suited for making security-related decisions.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Replacing a substring with itself has no effect and may indicate a mistake.
Using cookies without CSRF protection may allow malicious websites to submit requests on behalf of the user.
The 'else' clause of an 'if' statement should be aligned with the 'if' it belongs to.
